samples.summary: `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` is vacuous for the new `!readOnly &&` guard
samples.evidence: editor.ts now reports `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` / same for redo. The new read-only test builds `new MemNoteStore('hello')` and makes no successful write, so `store.canUndo()` is already `false` — the assertion holds identically with or without the new `!readOnly &&` clause. To discriminate, the test would need a store with real undo history (e.g. edit before mounting read-only, or a stub whose `canUndo()` returns true). Impact if the guard regresses: a viewer's toolbar offers an enabled Undo/Redo button that does nothing.

samples.summary: The new `if (readOnly) return;` in `runHistory` has no test that can fail if it is removed
samples.evidence: editor.test.ts's read-only test asserts `expect(undo).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` on a `vi.spyOn(store,'undo')`. But `initialize` now passes the `readOnlyNoteStore` proxy to `runHistory`, and the proxy maps `undo`/`redo` to `noHistory` without ever touching the target — so the spy stays uncalled, and the text stays 'hello', whether or not the `if (readOnly) return;` line exists. The guard is redundant defense that no assertion pins; the same test also cannot tell which of the two layers stopped the write.

samples.summary: Divider resize math change (`track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`) and the 25px / `touch-action: none` divider change are untested
samples.evidence: The diff changes the drag ratio denominator from `rect.width` to `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`, widens the divider 7px→25px and adds `touchAction: 'none'` — a user-visible split-pane behavior change whose stated motivation is that the handle previously trailed the pointer and could not be dragged by finger. `grep -n 'divider|split|resize'` over packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts returns no matches, and no other test in packages/notes references the divider or splitRatio. A jsdom test can at least assert the styles and, with a stubbed `getBoundingClientRect`/`offsetWidth`, the flex-basis produced by a synthetic pointerdown+pointermove.

samples.summary: `NotesView`'s new `readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw` wrap has no frontend test
samples.evidence: notes-view.tsx now wraps the YorkieNoteStore for read-only mounts, and `storeRef` is retyped to `NoteStore`. There is no notes-view test file (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/notes/* shows only notes-toolbar.test.tsx, notes-thumbnail.test.ts, yorkie-note-store.test.ts, notes-undo-integration.test.ts), and the one new test that renders this surface, shared-notes-layout.test.tsx, mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely. The wrapper itself is well tested in packages/notes, and `initialize()` wraps again, so the defect this would catch is contained (e.g. the thumbnail's `getText()` reading through the wrong handle) — but the frontend wiring is uncovered.

samples.summary: Shadow-log `target` formatting is only tested for a single well-formed attribute
samples.evidence: The new code maps over `body?.attributes ?? []` with `${attr?.key ?? '?'}:${attr?.verb ?? '?'}` and joins with ','. The new spec case ('names the document and verb it would have denied') passes exactly one attribute with both fields present, so the join separator, the empty-attributes case (`target=`) and the `?` fallbacks are unexercised. Failure mode is a malformed diagnostic line, not data loss.

No code path in `handleAuth` ever writes `token=` into a log string, so this assertion passes regardless of behavior — it is a regression tripwire rather than coverage. Harmless, but it should not be read as evidence that credential redaction is tested (e.g. it would not catch the raw token being logged under a different label).

samples.summary: Only view-mode non-persistence is tested; keymap and showAuthors changes are not
samples.evidence: The layout's documented contract is 'reads every localStorage preference, writes none'. shared-notes-layout.test.tsx asserts that only for `wafflebase:notes:viewMode` ('applies a view-mode change without persisting it'). Nothing asserts that toggling the keymap picker or the blame gutter leaves `wafflebase:notes:keymap` / `wafflebase:notes:showAuthors` untouched, nor that they are seeded from storage at all — so a later `writeKeymap`/`writeShowAuthors` added here would ship unnoticed, silently overwriting an anonymous visitor's per-browser preferences.
searchedFor: grep keymap/showAuthors in the test file

samples.summary: The reader-allowlist's core design claim — an unlisted/new member is neutered by default — is not tested
samples.evidence: read-only.ts documents that the allowlist exists so a `NoteStore` member added tomorrow fails closed. The tests only call the members that exist today (`editText`, `batch`, `recordSelectionForHistory`, `setLocalSelection`, `undo`, `redo`), so nothing pins that an unknown function-valued property comes back as the shared `noop` rather than the real method. A one-line test calling an ad-hoc method on a store subclass would cover it. `subscribePresence` — a listed reader — is likewise never exercised.

samples.summary: The `token` now threaded into `SharedNotesLayout` from shared-document is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: shared-document.tsx passes `token={token}` to the extracted layout; the layout test constructs the component directly with a literal token, so nothing verifies the caller actually supplies it. There is no shared-document.test.tsx (glob of packages/frontend/src/app/shared/* shows only shared-document.tsx, shared-header-status.tsx, shared-notes-layout.tsx and its test). If the prop were dropped, an editor-role share-link visitor would silently lose image upload with no failing test.
